tagline: Tell us your budget. We'll tell you what to buy.
saleBanner: Festival sale is live · Our picks are re-checked during the Great Indian Festival and Big Billion Days

categories.name: Phones
guide: Start with the processor and the screen, not the camera megapixels. A Snapdragon 6-series, 7-series or Dimensity 7000-series chip will stay smooth for years; Unisoc and Helio chips are fine for calls, WhatsApp and YouTube but slow down with heavy apps. An AMOLED screen is the single biggest upgrade you will notice every day.

Phone prices in India went up sharply in 2026 because memory chips got more expensive, so last year's models are often the better deal. That is why many of our picks are 2025 phones still in stock at lower prices, while some newer models are listed above their old price brackets.

Check how many years of software updates the brand promises, and whether there is a service centre near you. Samsung, Motorola, OnePlus and Google are the safest for long-term support. Ignore claims like 'up to 16GB RAM' — that counts storage used as virtual RAM, not real memory.

categories.name: Laptops
guide: Look at the processor and RAM first. For college and office work, a 13th-gen Core i3, Core 3, Ryzen 3 7000 or Ryzen 5 is enough; for coding, editing or many browser tabs, get 16GB RAM and an H-series chip (like the Core i5-13420H or Core 5 210H). Always pick an SSD, and check whether the RAM can be upgraded later, because many thin laptops have it soldered.

Laptop prices in India jumped in 2026 because memory chips got more expensive, so a Core i3 laptop that used to cost around ₹35,000 now sells for ₹45,000 or more. Under ₹35k the honest choices are Chromebooks, Android-based laptops or older Windows chips. If you need Windows for Office, coding or exams, stretching to about ₹45,000 gets you a laptop that will last.

Read the warranty line before you buy: onsite warranty means a technician comes to you, carry-in means you visit a service centre. Dell, HP, Lenovo, ASUS and Acer have the widest service networks. For gaming, the graphics card matters more than the processor: an RTX 2050 is entry level, an RTX 3050 handles most games at medium settings, and RTX 50-series cards run new games at high settings.

categories.name: Tablets
guide: Buy for the chip and the screen. A Snapdragon 6- or 7-series, Dimensity 7000-series, Helio G99 or Apple A16 keeps a tablet smooth for years; a 90Hz or 120Hz screen with at least 2K resolution makes reading and video noticeably nicer. Get 6GB RAM or more if you will split the screen or take notes alongside a video class.

Android or iPad? Android tablets from Samsung, Lenovo, Xiaomi, OnePlus and Motorola cost less and often include a stylus or keyboard support; Samsung promises the longest updates. The base iPad costs more but gets updates for 6+ years and has the best apps for drawing and note-taking, though the Apple Pencil and keyboard are extra.

Avoid unbranded or little-known tablets with 'up to 12GB RAM' claims: that counts virtual RAM, and buyer reviews show far more dead screens, charging faults and no service. Under ₹15k the only tablet we trust is the Lenovo Tab M11; spending around ₹18–22k gets a much better screen and chip.

categories.name: TVs
guide: Choose the size from where you sit: about 32 inches for a bedroom (under 6 feet), 43 inches for 6–8 feet, 55 inches for 8–10 feet and 65 inches beyond that. At 43 inches and up, get 4K; at 32 inches, Full HD or HD is fine. QLED gives brighter, richer colour than a plain LED panel; Mini LED and OLED are worth it only above ₹70k.

Panel failures are the biggest risk with TVs. In 1–3★ reviews on Amazon and Flipkart, the common complaints are lines on the screen, dead panels within a year and slow service visits. We dropped several popular models where more than about 1 in 8 buyers gave 1–2★, and kept brands with a wide service network: Samsung, Sony, Xiaomi, realme, Motorola, TCL.

Check the smart platform and ports. Google TV and Tizen get the most apps and updates. For a PS5 or Xbox, look for a 120Hz panel with HDMI 2.1 and ALLM. Built-in speakers are weak on almost every budget TV, so set aside money for a soundbar if dialogue clarity matters.

categories.name: Earbuds
guide: Decide first whether you need active noise cancelling (ANC). It blocks bus, train and office noise and is worth it if you commute; real ANC starts around ₹1,800 now. Without ANC, spend on battery life, comfort and a known brand instead. Ignore the big 'up to 100 hours' battery claims: that number includes the case, and each charge of the buds usually lasts 5–8 hours.

Cheap earbuds fail more often. Under ₹1,500, about 13–15% of buyers on Amazon and Flipkart rate their earbuds 1–2★, mostly because one bud stops working or charging after a few months. From ₹1,600 up, OnePlus and realme models drop to around 6–10%. Paying a little more for a brand with service centres, like OnePlus, realme, boAt, Samsung or Apple, makes warranty claims much easier.

Match the earbuds to your phone. AirPods work best with iPhones and Galaxy Buds with Samsung phones; most extra features are locked to their own brand. For running or cycling outdoors, open-ear or bone-conduction designs let you hear traffic. For gaming, look for a 'low latency' or 'game' mode of 50ms or less.

categories.name: Headphones
guide: Pick the type first. Bluetooth headphones are best for phones and travel; wired headphones never need charging, last for years and give better sound for the money; gaming headsets add a boom mic for team chat. Over-ear cups are more comfortable for long hours than on-ear ones, which press on your ears.

If you commute or work in a noisy place, get noise cancelling (ANC). The boAt Rockerz 512 ANC is the cheapest one we trust, the Sony WH-CH720N and JBL Tune 780NC are the sweet spot, and the Sony WH-1000XM5 and Bose QuietComfort are the best. If you record music or edit video, choose studio headphones like the Audio-Technica ATH-M20x or Sony MDR-7506: they sound flat and accurate rather than bassy.

Check the battery number honestly: 30–50 hours is plenty for most people, and anything over 60 hours usually means lower volume or ANC off. Sony, JBL, boAt and Bose have the widest service networks in India. For gaming on a PC or console, wired headsets from HyperX or Razer are more reliable and cheaper than wireless ones.

categories.name: Earphones
guide: Check your phone's port before buying wired earphones. Most new phones have no 3.5mm headphone jack, so you need a Type-C pair (or an adapter). Wired earphones are still the best value for calls, online classes and gaming, because they have no delay and no battery to wear out.

Neckbands sit between wired earphones and earbuds: they are hard to lose, last 25–40 hours and cost less than good earbuds. OnePlus and realme make the most reliable ones. If you want noise cancelling on a budget, a neckband like the realme Buds Wireless 5 ANC is cheaper than ANC earbuds.

For better music, look at in-ear monitors (IEMs) like the KZ EDC Pro or ZSN Pro X. They sound far clearer than typical earphones at the same price, but KZ is an imported brand sold through resellers, so service is limited. Cheap earphones under ₹500 wear out within a year for about 1 in 8 buyers, so treat them as replaceable.

categories.name: Soundbars
guide: Decide what is wrong with your TV's sound. If you cannot hear voices clearly, a 2.0 or 3.1 soundbar with a centre channel fixes it; if you want cinema bass, get a 2.1 bar with a subwoofer; for real surround sound, you need 5.1 with rear speakers. Ignore huge wattage numbers on cheap bars: a 100W Sony often sounds better than a '500W' budget bar.

Connect with HDMI ARC (or eARC) if your TV has it, so the TV remote controls the soundbar volume. Optical is the next best; Bluetooth adds a slight delay and lower quality. Check that the soundbar width suits your TV: a long bar under a 32-inch TV looks odd, and a tiny bar under a 65-inch TV sounds thin.

Under ₹5,000, most soundbars we checked had 15–25% of buyers rating them 1–2★, so we kept only a few. Between ₹5,000 and ₹10,000, boAt, Zebronics and Mivi give big sound for the money, and Sony gives the cleanest. Above ₹15,000, Sony dominates on reliability, with very few complaints in buyer reviews.

categories.name: Bluetooth Speakers
guide: Think about where you will use it. For travel, the bathroom or the beach, get an IP67 speaker like the JBL Go 3 that survives water and dust. For parties, size matters: bigger speakers with more watts and bigger drivers fill a room. For a desk or bedroom, a small speaker with good battery life is enough.

Battery claims are measured at low volume, so expect about half at party levels. TWS or 'party' pairing lets you join two speakers for stereo, and only works with the same brand. JBL, Sony, boAt, Marshall and Bose have the best service in India; imported brands like Tribit sound great but are harder to get repaired.

Under ₹2,000, boAt and Portronics are the most reliable; avoid unbranded 'tower' and 'party' speakers, which had 20–40% of buyers rating them 1–2★. Above ₹10,000, the Bose SoundLink Flex had the lowest complaint rate of any speaker we checked.

categories.name: Refrigerators
guide: Size the fridge by family: 80–100 L for a bachelor or hostel, 180–200 L for a couple, 230–260 L for a family of 3–4, and 300 L or more for bigger families. Single-door (direct cool) fridges are cheapest and use less power but need manual defrosting; double-door (frost free) fridges defrost themselves and keep vegetables fresher.

Choose an inverter compressor and the highest star rating you can afford, because a fridge runs 24 hours a day and power savings add up over 10 years. Convertible models let you turn the freezer into extra fridge space for festivals or parties. Samsung, LG and Whirlpool have the widest service networks in India.

Most bad fridge reviews on Amazon and Flipkart are about dents on delivery, late installation or stabilisers, not the fridge itself. Check the fridge carefully before the delivery person leaves, and use a stabiliser if your area has voltage swings. We dropped models where 1–2★ complaints were about the compressor or cooling failing.

categories.name: Washing Machines
guide: Pick the type first. Semi-automatic machines are cheapest and use the least water but need you to move clothes to the dryer tub. Top-load fully automatic machines are the easy middle ground. Front-load machines wash cleaner, are gentler on clothes and use less water and power, but cost more and take longer per cycle.

Size by family: 6–7kg suits 1–3 people, 7–8kg suits 3–5, and 9kg or more suits bigger families or anyone washing blankets at home. A built-in heater helps with stains and hard water, and an inverter (BLDC) motor runs quieter and lasts longer. LG, Samsung, IFB and Bosch had the fewest 1–2★ complaints in our check.

Most bad reviews on Amazon and Flipkart are about late installation, damaged delivery or service visits, not the machine itself, so check that the brand's service centre covers your pincode. If your area has hard water, a front-load with a heater or an anti-scale feature, plus a cheap inlet filter, prevents most drum and valve problems.

categories.name: ACs
guide: Size the AC by room: 1 ton for up to about 110 sq ft, 1.5 ton for 110–180 sq ft, and 2 ton above that or for top-floor rooms that get direct sun. Buy an inverter split AC; it cools faster, holds the temperature steadily and uses much less power than a fixed-speed model. Copper condenser coils are easier to repair than aluminium ones.

Star rating is about your power bill. If you run the AC 8 hours or more a day for most of the year, a 5-star model pays back its higher price within a few summers; for a few hours on hot nights, a 3-star is the better value. In our check, several premium 5-star models had more 1★ reviews than good 3-star ones, so a higher star rating does not mean a more reliable AC.

Most 1–3★ AC reviews are about installation: delays, extra charges for pipes and stands, and gas leaks from poor fitting. Confirm free installation, ask for the extra-pipe rate before the technician starts, and register the warranty yourself. Daikin, Voltas, Carrier, Panasonic and Midea had the best service feedback; we dropped models where complaints were about the unit failing, not the installation.

categories.name: Water Purifiers
guide: Check your water before you buy. If it comes from a borewell or tanker, or tastes salty, you need RO (reverse osmosis), which removes dissolved salts. If you get municipal water with low TDS (under 200), a UV + UF purifier is enough and wastes no water. A cheap TDS meter costs about ₹200 and tells you which you need.

The purifier price is only half the cost: filters need replacing every 12–18 months and cost ₹1,500–4,000 a year. Aquaguard, KENT, Pureit and Livpure have the widest service networks; Native by Urban Company and Atomberg use 2-year filters and need fewer service visits.

Avoid unbranded RO purifiers under ₹5,000, even with thousands of ratings. In our check they had 15–21% of buyers rating them 1–2★, with leaks, bad taste and no-show technicians. Most complaints even for good brands are about installation delays, so book installation as soon as the purifier arrives.

categories.name: Smartwatches
guide: Decide what you want the watch for. Under ₹5,000, smartwatches are mainly for notifications, calls and step counting; their heart-rate and SpO2 numbers are rough estimates. For accurate fitness tracking, GPS for runs or real apps like Google Maps and Wallet, spend ₹8,000 or more on Amazfit, OnePlus, Samsung, Apple or Garmin.

Budget smartwatches fail more often than any other gadget we track. In our check, many popular Fire-Boltt, Noise and boAt models had 15–22% of buyers rating them 1–2★, mostly for battery drain, dead screens and charging problems. We only kept models at about 12% or lower, and preferred brands with service centres like Samsung, Redmi, Fastrack and boAt.

Match the watch to your phone. Apple Watch works only with iPhone, and Wear OS watches like the OnePlus Watch 2R and Galaxy Watch8 work only with Android. Amazfit, Garmin, Redmi and most budget watches work with both. Look for an AMOLED screen, which is much brighter outdoors than LCD, and check the real battery life in reviews rather than the box claim.

categories.name: Watches
guide: Pick the style first. A steel-strap analog watch with a plain dial suits office and occasions; resin or silicone straps are better for sports, college and daily wear; digital watches like the Casio Vintage and G-Shock are the most practical. Titan, Casio, Fastrack, Sonata and Timex have service centres and battery replacement across India.

Check water resistance on the case back. '30m' or 'water resistant' only survives rain and hand washing; you need 100m or more to swim. Steel bracelets usually need a few links removed at a watch shop, which costs little. Leather straps look smart but wear out within a year or two if they get wet often.

Above ₹10,000, consider an automatic (self-winding) watch like the Seiko 5, which runs on your wrist movement and never needs a battery, or a solar Citizen Eco-Drive. Buy watches over ₹5,000 only from the brand's own store page or 'sold by' the brand on Amazon and Flipkart, because fake Fossil, Seiko and Tissot watches are common from third-party sellers.

categories.name: Power Banks
guide: Pick the capacity by use: 10,000 mAh charges a phone about twice and fits a pocket; 20,000 mAh charges 3–4 times and suits travel. Real usable capacity is about 60–65% of the number on the box, because some energy is lost as heat. Look for 22.5W or higher output with a USB-C PD port for fast charging.

Avoid power banks claiming huge capacities like 50,000 or 2,00,000 mAh for under ₹1,000. They are fake, and in our check such listings had over 20% of buyers rating them 1–2★. Xiaomi, Ambrane, Portronics, Spigen and Duracell had the most honest capacities and fewest complaints.

To charge a laptop, you need 45W or more from a USB-C PD port, and 65W for most bigger laptops. iPhone 12 and newer users can get a magnetic MagSafe bank for cable-free charging. Airlines allow power banks up to about 27,000 mAh (100Wh) in cabin baggage only, never in checked bags.

categories.name: Trimmers
guide: Decide what you want to trim. A beard trimmer with length settings is enough for most men; a multigroom kit adds attachments for hair, nose and body; Philips OneBlade trims, edges and shaves close without razor cuts, which suits stubble and clean-shaven looks. Waterproof trimmers can be rinsed and used in the shower.

Runtime matters if you trim often: 45–60 minutes is fine for weekly beard trims, while VGR and Havells models run up to 2–3 hours. Type-C charging means you can use your phone charger. Philips had the lowest complaint rates and the widest service network in our check.

Very cheap trimmers under ₹500 often pull hair and their batteries die within months; in our check some had over 20% of buyers rating them 1–2★. Spending ₹600–1,200 on Philips, Xiaomi, VGR, Havells or Bombay Shaving Company gets you a trimmer that lasts years.

categories.name: Monitors
guide: Match resolution to size: 24 inches is fine at Full HD (1080p), 27 inches looks sharper at QHD (1440p), and 4K is worth it at 27 inches or more if you edit photos, code all day or use a Mac. Choose an IPS panel for accurate colours and wide viewing angles; VA panels have deeper blacks but can smear in fast games.

For gaming, refresh rate matters most: 144Hz to 180Hz is a big jump over 60Hz and is now cheap. Office monitors at 100Hz or 120Hz still feel smoother for scrolling. Eye-care features like flicker-free backlight and low blue light are standard on BenQ, Dell and LG and help during long hours.

If you use a laptop, a USB-C monitor that charges it and carries the display over one cable is worth paying a little more for; check that it delivers at least 65W. Dell, LG, BenQ, Samsung and Acer have the widest service networks. Read the dead-pixel and warranty policy, because a few panel complaints show up for every brand.

categories.name: Office Chairs
guide: If you sit for more than 4–5 hours a day, buy a chair with adjustable lumbar (lower back) support and a mesh back, which stays cooler than foam in Indian summers. A headrest and a tilt that locks in more than one position matter once you work 8+ hours. Set the seat height so your feet are flat on the floor and your elbows rest at desk level.

Look past the huge discounts: many chairs show an MRP of ₹15,000–25,000 but sell for ₹3,000–4,500 every day. Judge them by the share of 1★ ratings instead. In our check, good chairs had 6–8% of buyers rating them 1★, while weak ones had 13–19%, mostly about broken tilt mechanisms, sinking gas lifts and warranty support that stops answering.

A 3-year warranty is common now, but it only helps if the brand answers. Godrej Interio, Green Soul, Wakefit and INNOWIN had the fewest service complaints. Most chairs arrive for DIY assembly in 20–30 minutes; check the chair for noise and wobble on day one, while the return window is open.

categories.name: Office Tables
guide: Measure first. A laptop needs a top of about 90 × 60 cm; a monitor, keyboard and laptop side by side need 120 × 60 cm. Depth matters more than people expect: under 50 cm puts a monitor too close to your eyes. Desk height should be 73–76 cm for most people with a normal office chair.

Most budget desks are engineered wood (particle board) on a metal frame. Thicker panels (18 mm) and a full metal frame wobble less when you type. Check reviews for wobble, chipped edges on delivery and missing screws, which were the most common complaints in our check.

Wakefit, DeckUp, Green Soul and FURLAY had the most consistent reviews. Wakefit includes free installation; most others are DIY and take 30–60 minutes. If your room doubles as a bedroom, a foldable or wall-mounted table gives the floor space back.

categories.name: Mattresses
guide: All prices here are for a Queen size (78 × 60 inches), the most common double bed in India. Measure your bed frame before ordering: some listings are 72 × 60 or 75 × 60, and a mattress that's too small leaves gaps at the edges. The same model costs about 15% less in Double size (72 × 48) and about 20% more in King (78 × 72).

For most people a medium-firm mattress is best, including for mild back pain. A very hard mattress is not better for your back. Memory foam reduces pressure on hips and shoulders and stops a partner's movement waking you; a dual-comfort mattress lets you flip between a soft and a firm side if you're unsure. Pick 6 inches or more if you weigh over 80 kg.

Most mattresses now come rolled in a box with a 100-night trial and a 7–10 year warranty. Wakefit, Sleepyhead/Duroflex and Sleepwell had the lowest share of 1★ ratings in our check (5–9%). Keep the box for the first few weeks in case you need to return it, and give it 2–3 weeks before deciding, since your body needs time to adjust.

categories.name: Air Purifiers
guide: Choose by CADR (clean air delivery rate), not the room size printed on the box. As a rule of thumb, you need about 1 m³/h of CADR per square foot of room for fast cleaning, so a 150 sq ft bedroom needs 150 m³/h or more and a 300 sq ft living room needs 250–300 m³/h. Always look for a True HEPA (H13) filter, which traps PM2.5 particles.

The real cost is the filter. Replacement filters cost ₹1,500–5,000 and last 6–18 months depending on how bad your air is and how long you run the purifier. Coway filters last the longest; check the filter price on the store before you buy the purifier.

Keep doors and windows closed while it runs, and place it at least a foot away from walls. Philips, Coway, Levoit and Cuckoo had the fewest 1★ ratings in our check (3–6%). Avoid cheap no-name purifiers that only list a coverage area and no CADR figure.
